key_insight: IrO2 is more stable than RuO2 because the rutile metal–oxygen bonds differ in their covalent and ionic character, which can be quantified from electronic structure descriptors.
engineering_relevance: These descriptors can guide the design of more durable, lower-cost OER catalysts by helping screen rutile oxides before synthesis.
method: Compared bulk rutile IrO2 and RuO2 electronic structures.
Analyzed metal–oxygen bond strengths to separate covalent and ionic contributions.
Used crystal-orbital-derived electronic descriptors across selected MO2 systems.
evidence_signal: The study is computational and comparative, using bulk electronic-structure analysis rather than experimental performance measurements to explain stability trends.
watch_item: Descriptor-based stability trends may not fully capture surface reconstruction, electrolyte effects, or real operating conditions in electrolyzers.
paper_title: The Stability of Rutile Oxides for Oxygen Evolution Catalysis: From Mechanistic Understanding to New Descriptors
